card.occupation: Vehicle technician (mechanic) at a small independent garage on an industrial estate between Castleford and Normanton. Does servicing, brakes, clutches and diagnostics, and is a qualified MOT tester. Full-time, roughly 40 to 45 hours a week, Monday to Friday plus alternate Saturday mornings.
card.education_detail: Left a local comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, including a pass in maths and English on the second attempt. Did a Level 3 apprenticeship in light vehicle maintenance and repair through a college in Wakefield, with day release while working at a fast-fit chain. Took his MOT tester qualification at 23 because the garage owner paid for it.
card.household: Rents a two-bed terraced house in Castleford with his girlfriend Chloe (26), a nursery practitioner. They have been together five years and living together for three. No kids. They have a staffie cross called Bruno. They have talked vaguely about getting engaged, but neither has pushed it.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in the Castleford and Pontefract area. His dad was a fitter at a glassworks and his mam works on the tills at a supermarket. He has one older sister who lives in Leeds with her family. The family isn't religious, and he's never given it much thought. He grew up with rugby league on the telly and in the local park.
card.professional_persona: Good with his hands and quick at diagnosing faults, but he doesn't enjoy dealing with customers and leaves the front desk to the owner whenever he can. He can be short with people who argue about a quote. He's not the tidiest worker: his bay is a mess, he forgets to log parts, and he's been told off more than once for leaving paperwork until Friday afternoon. The work itself is solid, though, and regulars ask for him by name.
card.sports_persona: Follows Castleford Tigers and goes to a few home games a season with his dad, though less than he used to. Played amateur rugby league until about 20 and stopped after a shoulder injury and a lack of motivation. Watches it on Sky now and doesn't play anything. He walks the dog most evenings, which is about the extent of his exercise.
card.arts_persona: Not into art in any formal sense. Listens to Arctic Monkeys, Kasabian and older indie, plus whatever's on Spotify in the garage. Watches crime documentaries and car restoration programmes on YouTube. Has been to a couple of gigs in Leeds, mainly because Chloe wanted to go.
card.travel_persona: Has been abroad a handful of times, mostly package holidays to Tenerife and Majorca and one lads' trip to Benidorm at 21 that he doesn't talk about much. He's happy with a week in a caravan at Filey or Whitby. Planning trips isn't his thing, so Chloe books everything.
card.culinary_persona: Calls the evening meal tea. Chloe does most of the cooking. When it's his turn it's usually pasta bake, a chilli, or a takeaway from the Chinese round the corner. He eats a meal deal or a sausage roll from Greggs at work most days, and likes a proper Sunday dinner at his mam's.
hobbies_and_interests: PlayStation, mostly FIFA/EA FC and Call of Duty online with two school mates
Coarse fishing at a local pond a few Sundays a month in summer
Tinkering with his own car, an older Ford Focus ST he keeps meaning to finish
skills: General DIY around the house, when he gets round to it
Fixing friends' and family's cars for cash or a few beers
card.career_goals: Hasn't got a firm plan. He half-thinks about going self-employed with his own mobile mechanic van, because he'd rather not have a boss, but he hasn't done anything about it. He'd also consider retraining on electric and hybrid vehicles if the garage paid for the course.
card.voice: West Yorkshire accent, fairly flat and unhurried. Short answers, often just a few words, and he won't elaborate unless prompted. Uses 'erm' a fair bit, and 'sort of' and 'to be fair' as hedges. Says 'mam', 'tea' for the evening meal, 'knackered' and 'mate'. Doesn't fill silences. He'll just wait for the next question, and can sound a bit blunt or bored without meaning anything by it. Occasionally ends with 'yeah' or 'do you know what I mean'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with minimal punctuation and often no full stop at the end. Drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im'). Short answers. Uses 'n/a' or 'dunno' when he can't be bothered. Sometimes uses 'tbh'. Occasional typos he doesn't fix.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit guarded. Polite enough but not warm, and he doesn't make small talk unless asked directly. Can come across as disinterested or slightly impatient, especially if questions seem pointless. Opens up a little if the topic is cars or rugby.
small_things: The dog chewed one of Chloe's shoes last week
Work has been mad busy with MOTs
Castleford lost again at the weekend
He's still waiting on a part for his own car
The Chinese round the corner has changed hands and isn't as good
He was knackered after a Saturday shift
deeper_things: He feels a bit stuck and wonders if this is it for the next 40 years
He's not sure he's ready to propose and feels some pressure from Chloe's family
His dad's health worries him since a heart scare last year
He's lost touch with most of his mates from rugby and feels a bit isolated
Money is tight with rent and bills going up, and he's a bit skint by the end of most months
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing his head and shoulders slightly off-centre to the left. Lit mainly by a ceiling light and the laptop screen, giving a flat, slightly cool light. Short brown hair cut close at the sides, a few days of stubble, a neutral and slightly tired expression with eyes looking just below the camera. No glasses. Wearing a grey hoodie with a small Nike logo. Behind him is a living room: a dark grey fabric settee with a folded throw on one arm, a magnetic wall with family photos slightly out of focus, a large TV on a black stand to the right with a PlayStation underneath, and the edge of a dog bed visible on the floor. The door to the hallway is ajar in the background.
